jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
Challenge Air for Kids & Friends, Inc.

Development Director

Full-Time | Dallas–Fort Worth, Texas

Are you a relationship builder who wants your fundraising work to make a meaningful difference in the lives of children and families?

Challenge Air for Kids and Friends Inc. is a Texas-based nonprofit that empowers children and young adults with physical and developmental challenges through the experience of flight. Through nationwide Fly Days, the organization partners with communities and families to offer youth ages 7 to 21 the chance to fly in small aircraft, with both wheelchair and non-wheelchair aviators. The program integrates elements of occupational, recreational, and educational therapy to help participants build confidence, overcome barriers, and expand their sense of possibility. Founded to give young people a new perspective from the sky, Challenge Air has inspired thousands to dream bigger and believe in their abilities.

The Development Director is a full-time hybrid role based in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, with a combination of on-site and work-from-home responsibilities. This role leads the planning, execution, and evaluation of fundraising strategies, including campaigns, events, and donor initiatives to support Challenge Air’s mission and programs. Day-to-day tasks include cultivating and stewarding individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations; managing donor communications; preparing proposals and grant applications; and maintaining accurate fundraising records and reports. The Development Director will collaborate closely with the CEO/Executive Director and program staff to align development goals with organizational priorities, oversee budgets related to development activities, and support board members and volunteers in fundraising efforts. The role also involves representing the organization at community events and Fly Days, strengthening relationships with stakeholders, and identifying new opportunities for philanthropic support.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Development Director will:
Develop and implement an annual fundraising and development plan.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors and prospective supporters.
Grow annual giving, recurring giving, major gift, and donor retention efforts.
Identify and develop corporate sponsorships and community partnerships.
Build relationships with donors, sponsors, foundations, service organizations, and community leaders.
Support foundation and grant fundraising efforts.
Manage donor communications, acknowledgments, stewardship, and recognition.
Maintain accurate donor and prospect information in the organization’s donor database/CRM.
Track fundraising progress and prepare reports to support planning and decision-making.
Work with the CEO/Executive Director, Board of Trustees, and volunteers to expand the organization’s fundraising reach.
Represent Challenge Air at Fly Days, community events, donor meetings, and networking opportunities.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Our ideal candidate is a confident and genuine relationship builder who enjoys connecting people with a meaningful mission. This person is strategic, organized, self-motivated, and comfortable working in a small nonprofit environment where everyone plays an important role.
Qualified candidates should have:
3 + years or more experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, sales, relationship management, or a related field.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Experience with donor databases, CRM systems, or similar technology.
The confidence and ability to cultivate donors and make direct fundraising asks.
The ability to work independently while collaborating closely with staff, board members, and volunteers.
A genuine commitment to the mission of Challenge Air for Kids & Friends.

WHY JOIN CHALLENGE AIR?

This is an opportunity to play a significant role in the growth of a national nonprofit organization with a unique and inspiring mission. The Development Director will have the opportunity to build relationships with donors and partners across the country while helping ensure that more children with special needs experience the confidence, joy, and possibilities created through the gift of flight.

To Apply:
Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in the position and relevant fundraising or relationship-development experience to HR @challengeair.org
.

Application Deadline: November 1, 2026

Salary Range: $65,000-$75,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications

Benefits: PTO, insurance, hybrid office position

Challenge Air for Kids & Friends, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Loomwork, an AI automation venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Loomwork is an AI automation agency for growing companies. Every growing company knows AI is its next growth lever, but few have the people to turn it into working systems. Implementation is the scarce resource. Loomwork helps them find where AI will pay off, builds agents into the tools they already use, and keeps those agents running. It launches as a services business with a dedicated technical delivery team from day one. Every engagement also serves as research: as client work converges on one segment, Loomwork turns its library of deployed agents into a connected product and grows from agency to software company.

Market Context

The global AI consulting services market is valued at $11.9B in 2026 and is projected to reach $73.9B by 2034, growing at a 25.6% CAGR. North America holds about 38% of the market. Enterprise AI adoption climbed from 20% in 2017 to 88% in 2025, and adoption is outpacing the talent available to deploy it. Roughly 190,000 US and Canadian companies fall in the $10M to $300M revenue range, which puts the serviceable market at an estimated $3B a year. Most of these companies are too large for freelancers and too small for enterprise firms.

jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

Department: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences – Marketing & Communications

Job Title: Assistant Director of Marketing and Communications

Position #: 00853105 – Requisition #: 41281

Job Summary:

This is an exciting opportunity for a collaborative and strategic marketing and communications leader to make a significant impact on the future of pharmacy education, research, and healthcare. Reporting directly to the Chief of Staff/Communications Director, the Assistant Director of Marketing and Communications will play a critical role in advancing the visibility, reputation, and strategic priorities of the Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences.

In this highly visible leadership role, the Assistant Director will oversee the daily operations of the Marketing and Communications Office and lead a talented multidisciplinary team responsible for content development, social media, web strategy, digital marketing, recruitment campaigns, CRM and email marketing, photography, video, and internal communications. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with faculty, academic program leaders, researchers, Student Services, and campus partners to develop and execute high-impact marketing and communications initiatives, strengthen the School's brand, improve operational effectiveness, and support emerging institutional priorities. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence strategic decision-making, mentor communications professionals, and drive meaningful engagement with prospective students, alumni, healthcare professionals, donors, and the broader community.

Key Responsibilities:

Develop, implement, and oversee integrated marketing and communications strategies that advance School priorities, increase visibility, strengthen brand awareness, and promote the School's educational programs, research, faculty expertise, and impact on healthcare and pharmacy practice.
Partner with academic programs, Student Services, and School leadership to develop and execute recruitment marketing initiatives that support enrollment goals for Doctor of Pharmacy, Master's, PhD, certificate, and other academic programs.
Oversee the day-to-day operations of the Marketing and Communications Office, including management of digital marketing, website, social media, content development, CRM and email marketing, and other communications platforms and technologies.
Directly supervise, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of marketing and communications professionals, fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing work environment aligned with School priorities and objectives.
Lead the planning, prioritization, and execution of multiple marketing and communications projects by establishing clear scopes, timelines, deliverables, workflows, and performance measures, while ensuring efficient use of staff and resources.
Serve as the primary operational liaison for marketing and communications activities across the School, building effective partnerships with faculty, staff, students, academic leaders, research leaders, Student Services, campus partners, and external stakeholders.
Collaborate closely with the Chief of Staff/Communications Director and School leadership to assess emerging opportunities and changing priorities, recommend strategic marketing and communications approaches, and adapt plans and resources to support the School's evolving goals and objectives.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, located at the Anschutz Medical Campus, is an internationally renowned School of Pharmacy and a top-tier research school ranked in the top 10% of more than 140 schools in the country for research grant funding. At the Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, we are committed to excellence and innovation in professional, graduate, and post-graduate education; scholarship and research; patient-centered care; public health advocacy; and societal leadership and engagement. Together, our innovation, discoveries, and engagement with our communities improve the health and well-being of society.

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation, and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Dental: Multiple plan options

Master's degree in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, or a related field.

Experience managing integrated marketing and communications campaigns across digital, web, social media, email, and traditional channels.

Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation communication skills.
Strong organizational, project management, and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously.
Demonstrated ability to lead, supervise, mentor, and develop professional staff in a collaborative team environment.

# Executive Director of Global Delivery

**Location:** United States / Hybrid or Remote  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time  
**Seniority Level:** Executive Director  
**Reports To:** Chief Operating Officer / Chief Executive Officer  

## About the Role

We are seeking an **Executive Director of Global Delivery** to lead the execution, coordination, and operational performance of the organization’s global delivery portfolio. This executive will oversee complex, multi-region initiatives, establish scalable delivery processes, and ensure that strategic projects and client commitments are executed with consistency, quality, and accountability.

The Executive Director will work closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to align delivery operations with business priorities, optimize resources, manage delivery risks, and strengthen organizational execution across markets.

## Key Responsibilities

### Global Delivery Leadership
- Lead global delivery operations across multiple regions, business units, and strategic initiatives.
- Establish delivery standards, operating processes, governance frameworks, and performance expectations.
- Translate executive strategy into actionable delivery plans, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
- Maintain executive-level visibility into delivery performance, priorities, risks, and dependencies.

### Portfolio & Program Delivery

### Team & Organizational Development
- Lead, develop, and scale global delivery teams and senior delivery leaders.
- Establish clear roles, responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability structures.
- Develop leadership capabilities across program management and delivery organizations.
- Foster a culture focused on ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and measurable results.

## Key Performance Areas

- Global delivery performance and execution

- Risk, issue, and dependency management

## Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Management, Technology, Engineering, or a related field.
- 15+ years of progressive experience in global delivery, operations, program management, professional services, consulting, technology, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience leading complex, multi-region programs and delivery organizations.
- Strong understanding of portfolio management, operational planning, delivery governance, resource management, and performance measurement.
- Experience managing senior teams across multiple functions, markets, or geographic regions.
- Strong executive communication, negotiation, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly cross-functional environment.

## Preferred Background

- Experience as an Executive Director, Senior Director, VP of Global Delivery, VP of Operations, Head of Delivery, or similar leadership role.

## What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means establishing a highly accountable and scalable global delivery organization that consistently converts strategic priorities into measurable business outcomes. The Executive Director will create greater visibility across the delivery portfolio, improve execution discipline, optimize resources, strengthen cross-functional coordination, and build a delivery organization capable of supporting long-term growth across multiple markets.

new_jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO — Supply Chain Tech | AI Returns Recovery
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Riuso, an AI recommerce venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Riuso is the operating record for electronics returns and liquidation benches. Owner-operated resellers and refurbishers spend around eleven minutes identifying, grading and pricing each returned or liquidated unit by hand. When the bench backs up, units default to the liquidation pallet, the lowest-value exit. Riuso identifies and grades each unit from photos in seconds and prices every disposition route, from resell and refurb to part-out, wholesale and pallet. It then routes the unit to the highest-recovery option. Every decision becomes memory the bench owns: repeat models price instantly, seller manifest accuracy builds over time, and outbound IMEI records turn mismatched returns into winnable claims. It runs on a phone and a label printer, with no integration.

Market Context

US consumers returned an estimated $849.9B of merchandise in 2025, and North American refurbished electronics is a roughly $17B market growing at double digits. Riuso addresses a $2.2B TAM across North American returns and recommerce benches. Its beachhead is 12,000 electronics-focused owner-operators, a $144M SAM. Right-to-repair laws now in force across California, New York, Texas, Oregon and five other states are deepening the parts market. Tariffs on new devices are pulling more buyers toward refurbished. Both make every unit on the bench worth more to price correctly.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across supply chain tech and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead execution.

Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with owner-operated electronics resellers and refurbishers, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct exposure to electronics resale, liquidation, refurbishment or reverse logistics

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

Community Forward SF is a collection of vital programs that ensures our neighbors experiencing homelessness have effective services designed for their unique needs. Whether one needs housing, medical shelter, a safe place for recovery, or calm in the face of domestic violence - we care for those most vulnerable in our community. We are not just one program. We are a network of programs designed to work together to meet every stage of need. We focus on the hardest-to-reach, most vulnerable people: Women, Medical Crisis, Substance Use Disorder, and Older Adults. Our programs meet the needs of people, rather than demanding that people meet the needs of our programs.

JOB SUMMARY:

Community Forward SF is hiring a Deputy Director of Subsidy Services (DDSS) for our Flexible Housing Subsidy Pool for the Ending Transgender Homelessness Initiative program. The program works with participants who are part of the trans and gender nonconforming community by providing case management, housing location and coordination services, and an ongoing housing subsidy.

The DDSS is responsible for oversight of housing services, including, but not limited to: team cohesion, supervision of Case Managers and a Housing Navigator, building and maintaining relationships with community partners with an emphasis on landlords, meeting regularly with the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and managing the programs’ contracts and budgets to ensure objectives are met and funds are spent appropriately.

Other duties as assigned

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Comparo, an AI-native residential appraisal venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Comparo is an AI-native residential appraisal firm built for independent mortgage banks and private lenders. Today, a lender waits 5 to 10 days for an appraisal that takes under an hour of real analytical work. Comparo collapses that to 24 hours. Homeowners or data collectors capture the property with a phone scan, AI selects comparables, runs adjustments and drafts the full report, and a licensed appraiser reviews and signs. Comparo sells the finished, UAD 3.6-compliant appraisal rather than software, so it owns the workflow end to end and captures the full per-report fee. FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Comparo, an AI-native residential appraisal venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Comparo is an AI-native residential appraisal firm built for independent mortgage banks and private lenders. Today, a lender waits 5 to 10 days for an appraisal that takes under an hour of real analytical work. Comparo collapses that to 24 hours. Homeowners or data collectors capture the property with a phone scan, AI selects comparables, runs adjustments and drafts the full report, and a licensed appraiser reviews and signs. Comparo sells the finished, UAD 3.6-compliant appraisal rather than software, so it owns the workflow end to end and captures the full per-report fee. The same engine extends to tax appeals, insurance, estate valuations and continuous portfolio revaluation for lenders and mortgage-backed asset holders.

Market Context

The US residential appraisal industry is an $8.8-11.4B market, with roughly 5 million appraisals completed each year at $400-700 per report. Mortgage appraisals ordered by independent mortgage banks and private lenders represent a $1.5-2.1B serviceable market. The timing is sharp: UAD 3.6 becomes mandatory on November 2, 2026, expanding each report from roughly 700 to 3,600 data fields, while an aging workforce of 75,000–80,000 licensed appraisers shrinks.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Weli, a B2B WealthTech venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Weli is an AI-native operations platform purpose-built for wealth management firms. It plugs directly into the CRM, portfolio management, and custodian systems firms already run, and executes the back-office work behind every account, account opening, money transfer, trade coordination, and compliance routing. Every wealth management firm already staffs an Operations function to do this work, typically at a ratio of roughly one Operations person to every three advisors, and that function is chronically stretched: slow, error-prone, and unable to give any single advisor's book the full attention it deserves. Weli is built for the firm's back office.

Market Context

Weli's customers are independent and hybrid RIAs, firms built around senior advisors who own their own client books and lean on a small, shared operations team to execute everything behind the scenes. It's a large and fast-growing world. There are roughly 300,000 wealth and financial advisors in the US, and the independent channel has been on a two-decade climb, from under a fifth of the industry's assets in 2007 to 27% today, on track for nearly a third by 2028.

Growth is outpacing the operations layer built to support it. The industry's leading benchmarking study found 78% of RIA firms were actively hiring last year just to keep up with capacity constraints, and most firms add a full new hire for every $360,000 of revenue growth, an expensive, linear way to scale a business that should compound. In our own interviews, one managing partner put a number on it directly: his firm could roughly triple its assets under management with its current advisor headcount if operations could keep pace. That gap, real, quantifiable, and largely unaddressed by today's AI tools, is Weli's opportunity.

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Associate Director of Development, Major Gifts (New York Regional Office)

Job Profile Title

Major Gifts Officer

Based in New York City and reporting to the Director of Development of the New York Regional Office, the Associate Director of Development, Major Gifts manages a personal portfolio of major gift prospects and donors in the New York region, identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individuals capable of making gifts of $100,000 or more to University priorities. The Associate Director devises fundraising strategies and regional cultivation/stewardship events and programs for their prospect pool, often in collaboration with other University colleagues, and engages volunteers to help build and steward relationships with alumni, parents, and friends of the University.

Job Description

This role is based in our New York office.

Job Responsibilities

Major Gifts Fund-raising

Responsibilities

Cultivate and solicit alumni donor prospects in the New York region, with emphasis on securing commitments of $100,000 or more to the University’s top priorities. Responsibilities include:

Manage a prospect pool of ~ 150-200 names
Identify and rate new prospects capable of making gifts of $100,000 or more.
Develop and implement individualized cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies for prospects and donors with an emphasis on increasing their financial commitment to the Penn Fund and University priorities.
Write gift proposals and other case building and stewardship materials as needed.
Represent the University at regional and on-campus events.

Collaboration with University Development Staff

Work closely with the Director of Development for Major Gifts on individual prospects, special events, and development of overall strategic plan for assigned donor prospect pool. Collaborate with campus-based colleagues including Penn Fund/Reunion Program, Principal Gifts, School/Center development officers, Gift Planning, and Alumni Relations staff.

Work closely with campus-based development colleagues to create and support events and programs (both regionally and on campus) that will lead to increased high-level involvement of alumni in the region as well as to develop individual strategies to cultivate and steward prospect interests across a variety of areas across the University.
Staff prospect visits for University leaders, e.g. President, Dean or faculty member, and by senior development officers; includes developing prospect briefing/goals and managing follow up actions.

Volunteer Management

Identify, recruit, train and support volunteers. Cultivate local alumni for future volunteer leadership roles at the University (e.g. boards of Trustees and Overseers, Advisory boards, reunion volunteers, speakers and other alumni leadership activities).

Work strategically with volunteers to encourage them to build bridges and utilize their networks to help Penn develop stronger relationships with other prominent alumni, parents, and friends of the University.
Engage volunteers in prospect identification and evaluation process
Oversee select prospect assignments to volunteers, including the provision of pre- and post-contact support and, as appropriate, accompanying volunteers on cultivation/solicitation visits.
Keep volunteers informed about the University and its fundraising priorities.
Please provide a resume and cover letter in order to be considered for this role. Please upload all documents in the “Resume/CV” section of the application prior to submitting.**

Bachelor Degree and 3 to 5 of successful fund-raising experience, preferably in higher education and in the New York metropolitan area, including direct solicitation of five and six figure gifts from individuals or equivalent combination of education and experience is required.
Familiarity with Penn and/or solid understanding of a major research university environment.
Excellent communication skills, both oral and written.
Ability to work independently, but collaboratively, in goal-oriented team environment.
Must be willing to travel and work evenings and weekends as needed (valid driver's license required)

New York, New York

Department / School

Development and Alumni Relations

$77,330.00 - $125,000.00 Annual Rate

Health, Life, and Flexible Spending Accounts: Penn offers comprehensive medical, prescription, behavioral health, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits to protect you and your family’s health and welfare. You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.

Company Description
Breaking Free is a long-standing leader in the anti-trafficking movement, supporting survivors of sex trafficking and commercial sexual exploitation since 1996. The organization offers a holistic model of care, including survivor advocacy, long-term safe housing, trauma-informed healing programs, policy change efforts, and accountability services for purchasers. Rooted in the voices and lived experiences of survivors, Breaking Free focuses on creating pathways to safety, justice, and lasting change. The organization works to dismantle systems of exploitation and build a future where all people can live with dignity, independence, and the freedom to realize their full potential. Team members join a mission-driven environment dedicated to survivor-centered, equity-focused practice.
Role Description
The Executive Director is a full-time, hybrid role based in St Paul, MN, with flexibility for some work from home. This role provides overall strategic and operational leadership for Breaking Free, including setting organizational vision, guiding program development, and ensuring alignment with the mission and survivor-centered values. new_jobs.description:

JOB OBJECTIVE

The Executive Director will be a leader with the presence to effectively lead and advance the priorities established by the National Child Support Engagement Association (NCSEA) Board of Directors. The position requires effective management experience, fiscal responsibility, and success working with associations, industry partners, stakeholder groups, and policy makers on behalf of those that are the voice of the child support community.

Serving as the association's chief executive, the Executive Director partners with the NCSEA Board of Directors to advance the association's mission, execute its strategic plan, and deliver exceptional value to members. This role provides leadership for revenue growth, financial performance, governance, and staff excellence.

As a member of the MCI USA team, the Executive Director is equally accountable for the health of the NCSEA account within MCI's full-service management portfolio. The role stewards a win-win partnership in which NCSEA receives exceptional value and measurable results, and MCI earns a fair, sustainable return through disciplined scope, resource, and contract management.

COMPENSATION:
$90,000-95,000 annually, based on relevant experience and skills.

Responsibilities

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

Revenue Growth:

Develops, in partnership with designated NCSEA Board of Directors and sponsorship and resource development staff, an overall resource development plan that will generate both program and operational funding.
Oversees the Corporate Partner program, working with the Fundraising and Partnerships Manager, to maintain relationships, create benefits, and sustain growth of the partner program.
Networks with current and prospective corporate partners and sponsors at conferences and other industry events to enhance engagement and expand revenue opportunities.
Actively solicits new corporate partnerships and sponsorships aligned with NCSEA’s mission and priorities.
Collaborates with the Membership and relevant corporate relations/partnership committees to strengthen the value proposition for members and partners, including benefits, programming, and engagement opportunities.

Governance, Management And Administration

Monitors the day-to-day delivery of the organization's programs and services to maintain or improve quality.
Serves as chief staff executive for NCSEA with responsibility of staff management and oversight.
Assists the NCSEA Board President and Board of Directors in the development and implementation of the NCSEA Strategic Plan and Annual Business Plan and in the creation of policies, procedures, and updates to the Policy Manual as needed but no less than annually.
Supports the NCSEA Board of Directors by working collaboratively with the President, officers, and committee chairs and by routinely providing staff reports and data as needed. Related tasks include providing staff support for the Board of Directors and assigned committees, including scheduling meetings, developing recommended meeting agenda and meeting materials, and developing resource materials.
Works with the Board of Directors or at Board direction with other designated individuals or organizations to facilitate NCSEA's link with research to promote program goals.
Serves as the liaison with other organizations, including ERICSA (Eastern Regional Interstate Child Support Association), NCSL (National Conference of State Legislatures), NTCSA (National Tribal Child Support Association), NATCSD (National Association of Tribal Child Support Directors), NCCSD (National Council of Child Support Directors), WICSEC (Western Intergovernmental Child Support Engagement Council), the Federal Office of Child Support Enforcement (OCSE), and the American Public Human Services Association (APHSA).
Prepare Board of Directors for election process, including communication, processing and database management.
Monitors and ensures the content on the NCSEA website is current and best represents the association.

Advocacy And Education

Leads conference planning for in-person and virtual events, in coordination with the Executive Committee, including third party contracting, onsite coordination, and scripting for executive leadership.
Works with NCSEA’s legislative advocate to implement recommendations and actions as directed by the appropriate NCSEA committees and Board of Directors.
Coordinates NCSEA’s efforts to impact and inform policy and legislation at the federal, local, and international levels, in conjunction with the President, the Policy and Government Relations Committee, and the Board of Directors as appropriate

Fiscal

Provides primary oversight of NCSEA’s budget, ensuring alignment with the Strategic Plan and Annual Business Plan, and partnering with the Treasurer and Finance Committee on development, monitoring, and timely adjustments.
In coordination with the Treasurer, manages finances, budgets, processes, and procedures; reviews finances for Board of Directors’ reports; and monitors for needed adjustments to NCSEA’s budget or investment portfolio.
Oversees the administration of the funds of the organization according to the approved budget, and monitors the cash flow of the organization.
Ensures that the Finance Committee and Board of Directors are provided with comprehensive, regular reports on the revenues and expenditures of the organization.

Account Management & Partnership Stewardship (MCI)

Ensure a strong, productive, and mutually beneficial relationship between NCSEA and MCI USA, maintaining a high level of trust, service, and collaboration.
Manage the NCSEA resources in alignment with the contracted scope of services, approved staffing model, service expectations, and financial objectives.
Partner with MCI USA leadership to monitor account performance, resource allocation, service delivery, and overall account sustainability, proactively identifying opportunities to strengthen results and partnership value.
Identify and elevate potential scope changes, capacity constraints, service-level concerns, or emerging risks, and collaborate with MCI leadership on appropriate solutions.
Contribute operational insight and recommendations that support contract stewardship, long-term partnership success, and future planning discussions between NCSEA and MCI USA.
Maintain awareness of MCI USA capabilities and, when appropriate, identify opportunities that could enhance member value, organizational effectiveness, or NCSEA strategic objectives.
Model the win-win partnership philosophy by balancing advocacy for NCSEA's mission and priorities with responsible stewardship of MCI USA resources and commitments.

Staff Leadership

Provide leadership and oversight of the NCSEA-designated staff team, fostering a high-performing, engaged, and accountable culture aligned with organizational goals, incorporating feedback from NCSEA volunteers.
In partnership with MCI's People and Culture team, support talent management efforts including recruitment, onboarding, coaching, performance management, professional development, succession planning, and retention.
Establish clear goals, performance expectations, and accountability measures that drive results and continuous improvement.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and oversight of the NCSEA-designated staff team, ensuring clear priorities, effective collaboration, and accountable execution of NCSEA programs and services.
Participate in and support a 360-degree feedback process to strengthen leadership effectiveness, team performance, and the partnership between NCSEA and MCI.
All other duties as assigned

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree required.
Minimum 5 years of progressive association management experience.
Demonstrated progressive management experience in an association or non-profit organization.
Ability to engage participation from all levels, and generate passion for the association’s work, both internally and externally.
Association Management Company (AMC) experience is preferred.

PROFESSIONAL AND LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES

Outstanding written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills including engaging public speaking.
Collegial, collaborative style.
Exceptional organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and complex projects in a fast-paced environment.
Good decision-making skills, tactful, good listener, willingness to search out answers, ability to recognize when others need to be involved in activities or decisions.
Creativity, curiosity, empathy, high-energy level, and an enthusiasm for meeting and working with a wide range of individuals.
Ability to engage participation and build trust with volunteers, members, staff, and MCI leadership.
Sound judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to navigate the dual accountability of serving a client board while representing MCI's interests.

Specific Technical Skills

Curiosity and vision in applying AI, digital innovations, and emerging technologies to strengthen association programs and services.
Experience with the full Microsoft Office suite.

Additional Requirements

The position requires occasional evening and weekend work and domestic travel, approximately 3 to 5 trips per year, including NCSEA’s Leadership Symposium and Public Policy Summit.

MCI USA is an established, family-friendly company offering outstanding benefits and significant growth opportunities.

PTO
13 paid company holidays, including closure Christmas Eve through New Year’s Day
401K
Medical, dental, vision and supplementary insurances
Employer-paid group life insurance, short-term and long-term disability
Employer-paid family building benefit (fertility, adoption and surrogacy)

Pet discount program

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment with equal opportunities for everyone, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, age or physical/mental ability.

We appreciate all who apply, though only those selected for an interview will be contacted. All applications remain confidential. MCI USA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. If you need any accommodations during the application or interview process, please reach out to our chief people officer.

Conventions, workshops, and one day events
National level meetings (townhalls, webinars, etc.)

Work with divisional boards to create a meeting cadence and schedule accordingly

Experience working with volunteer leaders, boards, committees, or other stakeholder groups
Experience coordinating events, programs, meetings, or educational activities
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and responsibilities independently
Strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal skills
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite

Experience with membership management or association management systems
Experience managing social media platforms, including Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn

Experience with budgeting, expense management, and financial reporting

new_jobs.title: Managing Director
new_jobs.description:
The Organization:

Movement Labs is a program incubator and consulting firm that uses technology, data, and randomized controlled trials to win elections and build progressive power. Since 2017 we have run more than 250 RCTs on voter behavior.

We operate the largest evidence-based political texting programs in the country and incubate new electoral tactics - from Contest Every Race, which recruits Democratic candidates and supports 400+ local Democratic parties, to neighborhood captains, comedy persuasion, and organic social media. We are 110 staff in the 2026 cycle, fully remote, and aim to grow ~2x for the 27-28 cycle.

The Opportunity :

We are building the next generation of political infrastructure. Your job is to create the organizational leverage that lets exceptional teams execute.

This is fundamentally a scaling role. You report directly to the founder and CEO, who will continue to focus his energy on strategy, fundraising, new programs, and the greatest opportunities for impact. You will ensure that the organization itself is built to support those goals.

You have personally helped take an organization, business, or program through significant growth and understand what has to change as scale increases. You know how to translate growth strategy into operating reality: the structures, leadership capacity, management practices, planning rhythms, and decision rights that let a larger organization stay fast and effective.

The Leader:

The title Managing Director is intentionally broad. We are open to different leadership profiles and will shape the role around your strengths.

You might be a highly strategic chief-of-staff-type leader
: an exceptional generalist who runs the leadership team, drives priorities and decisions, solves complex cross-organizational problems, and serves as a close thought partner and proxy to the founder.

You might be a more operational COO-type leader
with direct responsibility for functions such as people, finance, legal, operations, technology, or program delivery.

Many compelling candidates will sit somewhere between those two profiles.
What is not flexible is the core mandate: create the organizational leverage, operating discipline, and leadership infrastructure that will enable us to approximately double in size while preserving the speed, experimentation, high standards, and mission focus that have made us successful.

What success looks like in year one:

By Q2 2027, the 2027–28 plan and budget is robust, with clear choices and flex points, and has genuine buy-in from the leadership team.
The organization has the structure, leadership capacity, decision rights, and operating systems required to execute the 2028 plan at approximately twice its current scale and net 1 point of presidential vote share in key states.
Existing and new staff can sprint on the most promising tests ahead of 2028 without organizational bottlenecks slowing execution.
Every VP understands what they own, what they can decide, where they need alignment, and how their work connects to organization-wide priorities.
The leadership team operates on a predictable planning and decision cadence; cross-functional problems are surfaced and resolved quickly, and issues reach you before they need to reach the CEO.
Communication and culture practices scale with the organization, ensuring that crucial program, business, and organizational information reaches staff clearly and consistently.
The CEO spends substantially more time on strategy, fundraising, new programs, and big swings because you run the organization day to day.

What You’ll Own:

The Core Mandate…

Scale the organization.
Translate the 2x growth strategy into an organizational and operating model that can support it. Anticipate what will break at the next stage of scale and build the people, processes, systems, and decision structures before they become constraints.
Lead the leadership team.
Run the weekly leadership cadence, quarterly goal-setting, planning, and organization-wide decision processes. Create clarity around priorities, owners, timelines, budgets, and tradeoffs.
Manage and develop senior leaders.
Directly manage a portfolio of VPs and/or directors, strengthen management quality across the organization, and build leadership capacity for a substantially larger enterprise.
Design the organization.
Shape structures, roles, accountabilities, cross-functional interfaces, and management rituals for a fast-growing, fully remote organization while protecting a high-performance, mission-driven culture.
Serve as the CEO’s strategic partner and proxy.
Help evaluate major investments and opportunities on both mission and business terms; resolve difficult internal questions; unstick decisions; mediate across teams; and turn strategy into execution.
Operate at election-cycle speed.
Create enough structure to support scale without bureaucracy that slows us down, and help teams decide well and fast when priorities shift.

Scope Shaped Around You….

We are hiring first for excellence against the core scaling mandate and will finalize the org chart around you. You will directly own - or work closely with the leaders responsible for – some combination of:

People and operations:
hiring, onboarding, performance and growth systems, HR, organizational operations, and labor relations with the staff union.
Finance:
budgeting, projections, cash and margin across multiple entities (LLC, PAC, c4, c3), working with finance consultants or partnering with a standalone CFO.
Legal and compliance:
partnership with General Counsel on contracts, compliance, entity structure, and labor matters.
Core programs and technology:
teams designing and delivering established programs, particularly SMS turnout work.
Consulting and partnerships:
teams selling and delivering electoral and advocacy programs for campaigns, PACs, and partner organizations.
New program lines and growth opportunities:
including organic social media, field, warmed audiences, volunteer organizing, paid advertising, and potentially small-dollar fundraising.

Is This You?

Required

10+ years of professional experience, including substantial experience managing managers and senior leaders in a high-performance environment.
Demonstrated experience helping lead an organization, business, program, or major function through significant growth - ideally 2x or more - and personal ownership of the operational or organizational changes required to make that growth work.
A builder’s understanding of scale: you have created or materially improved structures, roles, management systems, and operating rhythms rather than inheriting them.
Exceptional judgment and general-management range. You move comfortably between strategy, people, operations, and execution; you have structured and hired roles to create leverage and built accountability without unnecessary bureaucracy.
Deep motivation to work in the democracy space, and comfort with the urgency and intense sprints the election calendar creates.
Ability to bring the right amount of order to an entrepreneurial environment: rigorous where rigor creates leverage, flexible where speed and experimentation matter.

Beneficial

Political campaign, party, or political-tech experience is a real advantage, though we have hired great leaders here without it. Advocacy, civic engagement, or other fast-moving mission-driven experience also helps.
Strategy consulting or similar analytical training followed by meaningful operating responsibility.
Experience in an evidence-driven organization where results are measured rigorously and resources are reallocated based on what works.
Experience with tech-enabled or performance-marketing programs; SMS experience is particularly relevant.
Experience with a unionized workforce.

Location:

Fully remote, with travel for leadership retreats and key meetings.

Compensation & Benefits:

Salary: $200,000–$250,000, depending on experience and location, with additional incentive compensation tied to successfully achieving Movement Labs' growth and impact goals.

Benefits: Health, dental, and vision; 401(k); work-from-home stipend; unlimited PTO.

Start date:

Target January 2027; flexible for the right candidate.

**If you are interested in this opportunity, please submit a resume and max. 500-word response to the following (please share the response direct to tory.clarke@bridgepartnersllc.com)

Share an example of a time you helped operationally scale a team, product, program, or organization.

What needed to change to support growth, what objectives were you working toward, who were the key stakeholders, what role did you personally play, and how did you navigate competing priorities along the way?

new_jobs.description:
NOTE: Clicking the "Apply" button on the City of Omaha job board will open a website where applications for this position must be submitted.

Below is a brief summary of the position. To learn more about the job, the Omaha Streetcar Authority, the City of Omaha, and the project, view the brochure .

Executive Director - Omaha Streetcar Authority

Salary
: $187,000–$222,000 annually (commensurate with qualifications)

The Omaha Streetcar Authority (OSA) seeks an innovative, strategic, and dedicated executive leader to serve as its Executive Director. Created through an interlocal agreement between the City of Omaha and Metro Transit, the OSA is charged with directing and implementing policies, plans, and operations for Omaha’s modern 3-mile streetcar system – a transformational infrastructure project connecting Downtown Omaha and the Blackstone District while driving billions in economic development. Reporting directly to the Omaha Streetcar Authority Board, this executive leader will exercise considerable independence in leading capital construction, transit operations, financial stewardship, and strategic urban growth.

New to Omaha?

Omaha offers the best of both worlds: the economic strength and amenities of a thriving metropolitan area paired with the welcoming spirit, affordability, and sense of community of a mid-sized city. Consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to live, Omaha is home to nearly 500,000 residents and a metro population of 1 million. The city boasts a resilient economy anchored by Fortune 500 companies such as Berkshire Hathaway, Mutual of Omaha, Union Pacific, and Kiewit Corporation.

Residents enjoy a low cost of living, short commutes, excellent schools, and vibrant, walkable urban and suburban neighborhoods. Major civic investments continue to transform the city, including the revitalized downtown Riverfront, which connects green spaces with the historic Old Market district. Omaha delivers world-class cultural attractions—including the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium, Joslyn Art Museum, Steelhouse Omaha, and the Men’s College World Series—backed by a strong tradition of philanthropy and public-private collaboration that supports ambitious civic and infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

Provide Strategic Leadership & Oversight: Direct daily operations of the OSA and its operations/management contractor. Prepare long-term financing proposals, operating plans, and strategic initiatives for consideration by the OSA Board.
Oversee Capital Projects & Construction: Lead capital construction, track systems, overhead wires, and facility development—including the Vehicle Maintenance Facility—while monitoring contracts to ensure on-time performance, preventative maintenance, and strict performance metrics.
Manage Fiscal Operations & Revenue: Administer budget allocations, evaluate operating and general streetcar funds, assess project needs, and oversee bond data preparation and fiscal audits in collaboration with the City of Omaha. Pursue revenue generation through streetcar sponsorships and advertising.
Ensure Regulatory & Safety Compliance: Serve as the designated Accountable Executive for Transit Asset Management (TAM) and Public Transportation Agency Safety Plans (PTASP) under Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regulations. Maintain full compliance with ADA, Title VI, National Transit Database (NTD) reporting, and State Safety Oversight obligations.
Foster Economic Development & Partnerships: Drive policies that encourage complementary development along the streetcar corridor. Serve as the primary interlocal liaison between the City of Omaha and Metro Transit, while cultivating strong working alliances with business leaders, elected officials, regional partners, and community stakeholders.
Secure Grants & Lead Public Relations: Research, write, and manage federal and state grant opportunities. Serve as the chief media representative and spokesperson to promote the streetcar system, advance transit-oriented development, and advocate for sustainable transportation options.

Desired Qualifications

Qualified Candidates Will Demonstrate

Executive Experience: Seven (7) years of progressively responsible administrative and management experience in business administration, transportation planning, urban planning, or government relations, with significant executive leadership in the public or non-profit sector.
Technical & Regulatory Expertise: Strong knowledge of Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regulations, public transit operations, safety/risk management programs, contract administration, and federal grant specifications.
Fiscal & Development Acumen: Comprehensive understanding of municipal finance, redevelopment financing (including TIF), enterprise funding, budget preparation, and strategies for soliciting advertising and sponsorship revenue.
Strategic & Political Acumen: Proven ability to build consensus across governmental bodies, serve as a trusted liaison between public and private entities, and effectively communicate complex plans to elected officials, media, and the public.
Education & Credentials: A Bachelor’s degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Transportation Management, Transportation Planning, Urban Planning, or a related field is required. A Master’s degree is preferred. Possession of, or the ability to obtain, a valid driver’s license is required.

Compensation & Benefits

The expected salary range for this full-time, exempt position is $187,000–$222,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

The Position Offers a Competitive Executive Benefits Package, Including

Comprehensive health insurance with major medical, dental, and vision coverage
City/Authority contributions toward a Health Savings Account (HSA)
Defined benefit pension or municipal retirement program
Paid holidays, generous vacation, and sick leave allowance.

Location & Working Conditions

This position is based in Omaha, Nebraska. Work is primarily performed in an office setting, with regular field inspections required across active transit corridors, maintenance facilities, tracks, overhead wire systems, and aboard streetcar vehicles.

How To Apply

To be considered for this executive career opportunity, please submit your cover letter, resume, and six professional references. Resumes should clearly detail total years and months of employment history, specific employment start/end dates, and the scope of staff and budgets managed. References will not be contacted without prior candidate notification. Submissions are accepted online at https://hr.omaha.gov/executive-director-osa .

For Additional Information Regarding This Position, Please Contact

Mary Policky

Recruiting & Training Coordinator

mary.policky@cityofomaha.org

Application Deadline
: Sunday, November 1, 2026

The City of Omaha and the Omaha Streetcar Authority are Equal Opportunity Employers committed to non-discrimination, public stewardship, and providing accessible, sustainable, and high-quality transit infrastructure for the Omaha community.

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
Founded in 1995, CarePoint is a physician-owned, physician-run multispecialty medical group headquartered in the Denver metro area. What began as an emergency medicine practice has grown over three decades into a multi-state organization spanning emergency medicine, hospitalist medicine, pediatric emergency medicine, neurology, neurosurgery, physical medicine and rehabilitation, wound care, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and telehealth services. CarePoint's more than 600 physicians and advanced practice providers serve hospitals, health systems, and communities across Colorado, Kansas, Utah, Idaho, and Montana. The organization operates under a democratic, physician-led governance model and has built its reputation on long-standing hospital partnerships and a collaborative, collegial culture centered on high-quality, patient-focused care.

Position Summary

The Chief Operating Officer will provide operational leadership across CarePoint's multi-state footprint, ensuring consistent execution of clinical and business operations across diverse markets and practice settings. This role will partner closely with the Chief Medical Officer to align operational strategy with clinical quality, care delivery standards, and physician practice performance—ensuring that operational decisions strengthen, rather than compete with, clinical priorities.

The COO will own end-to-end operational performance: practice operations and workflow standardization, technology and infrastructure investments, administrative efficiency, talent and organizational development across sites, and the operational integration of new markets or acquisitions. They will partner with the CFO and CEO on contracting, payor relations and revenue cycle management. The COO will serve as a key architect of how CarePoint scales its physician-owned model while preserving the autonomy and culture that differentiate it in each market it serves.

Position Details

Status: Full-time, exempt
Location: Denver, Colorado, or Salt Lake City, Utah
Work Arrangement: Hybrid — a mix of in-person and remote
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Position Requirements

Education

Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or a related field is required.
An MBA or Master's in Healthcare Administration is required.

Experience

Minimum of seven years of progressive healthcare management experience, including at least five years in a senior enterprise or multi-site operations role.
Experience operating across multiple states or regions within a physician group, hospital system, or multispecialty healthcare organization.
Direct or matrixed leadership experience overseeing functional operational units (e.g., IT, HR, Marketing) is expected.
Experience leading payer and hospital/health system contract negotiations, ideally across multiple service lines.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Comprehensive understanding of healthcare operational and regulatory standards, and industry best practices across multiple states.
Ability to build trust and thought partnership with multispecialty physician leaders across a multi-state footprint.
Advanced knowledge of healthcare contracting, payer relations, and negotiation strategy across emergency medicine, hospitalist, and other specialty service lines.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and hold accountable senior operational leaders across divisions.
Strong financial acumen, including budget development, cost-control principles, and the ability to translate financial data into strategic recommendations.
Executive presence and communication skills, including experience presenting to and advising a Board of Directors.
Capacity to lead enterprise-wide strategic initiatives and manage change across a complex, multiple division organization.

Job Responsibilities

Divisional Oversight & Team Leadership

Provide operational oversight of each division, ensuring alignment with CarePoint’s mission, quality standards, and strategic goals.
Direct, coach, and manage company leaders who oversee each division, setting clear performance expectations and providing ongoing development.
Oversee the management of administrative teams, ensuring these functions effectively support enterprise operations and divisional needs.

Regional & Strategic Partnership

Serve as a strategic thought partner across the enterprise providing data and insight to support local decision-making.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with physician leadership across all regions to ensure operational alignment and trust.
Contribute to enterprise-wide strategy and cross-functional decision-making as an active member of the senior leadership team.
Provide strategic guidance and regular reporting to the Board of Directors on operational performance, contract status, and strategic priorities.
Lead execution of key strategic initiatives on behalf of the CEO and senior leadership team.

Contract Negotiation & Pro Forma Development

Lead contract negotiations for the Emergency Medicine, Hospitalist, Pediatric Emergency Medicine, Neurosurgery, PM&R, Hyperbaric, and Wound Care divisions.
Lead pro forma development for new and existing contracts, working with Finance's functional templates, actuals, and scenario models.
Monitor contract performance and renewal timelines, and negotiate favorable terms with hospital, health system, and payer partners.

Financial & Operational Management

Provide oversight to ensure divisions and corporate departments remain within their approved budgets, partnering with divisional leaders and the CFO on any clinical variances.
Conduct regular financial and operational analysis to identify areas for improvement, cost-saving opportunities, and growth potential.
Ensure all divisions adhere to local, state, and federal healthcare regulations and industry standards.
Represent CarePoint in public forums, industry associations, and partnerships to enhance the organization's reputation and influence.

Position: Regional Executive Director – East & Midwest

Classification: Salary, Exempt

Reports to: CEO

Summary/Objective

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Regional Executive Director – East & Midwest will run the day-to-day operations of the New England, Eastern, Mid-Atlantic, Middle States and Midwest Divisions for the Racquet Sports Professionals Association (RSPA). This position is responsible for all administrative tasks associated with the Divisions. The Regional ED (Executive Director) will work alongside the volunteer President and Division Board of Directors. The Regional ED will serve as a liaison to the RSPA network on a national, divisional, and regional level and to the divisional committees.

This position will be full-time, requiring 40 hours per week, with approximately 2–4 traveling weekends per year. new_jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO — InsurTech | AI-Native Insurance Brokerage
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Keystead, an AI-native insurance brokerage venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Keystead is an insurance brokerage built for the small businesses traditional brokers can't afford to serve. AI agents run the full workflow, from intake and multi-carrier quoting to binding and certificates of insurance, with licensed agents stepping in where judgment matters. Keystead starts with the businesses that need proof of coverage again and again, such as contractors, event vendors, and product brands selling into retail. For these owners, a certificate that takes days to arrive can cost them the job. Keystead issues it in minutes, explains coverage in plain language, and re-shops the market at every renewal.

Market Context

Roughly 35M small businesses in the US are underserved by a broker model built for larger accounts. Across the US and Canada, small business insurance represents a $6.2B commission pool. About $4.5B of that comes from businesses that already carry commercial insurance. Digital buying is proven, with the leading digital insurer serving more than 750K small businesses. The multi-carrier, servicing-first model remains open.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across insurtech and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead execution.

Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
Customer Development — Lead pilots with small business owners in certificate-heavy verticals, convert them to bound policies, and build the go-to-market motion
Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct exposure to commercial P&C insurance distribution, such as agency, brokerage, MGA, or insurtech experience, ideally with carrier relationships or a producer license

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

new_jobs.title: Development Director
new_jobs.description:
Challenge Air for Kids & Friends, Inc.

Development Director

Full-Time | Dallas–Fort Worth, Texas

Are you a relationship builder who wants your fundraising work to make a meaningful difference in the lives of children and families?

Challenge Air for Kids and Friends Inc. is a Texas-based nonprofit that empowers children and young adults with physical and developmental challenges through the experience of flight. Through nationwide Fly Days, the organization partners with communities and families to offer youth ages 7 to 21 the chance to fly in small aircraft, with both wheelchair and non-wheelchair aviators. The program integrates elements of occupational, recreational, and educational therapy to help participants build confidence, overcome barriers, and expand their sense of possibility. Founded to give young people a new perspective from the sky, Challenge Air has inspired thousands to dream bigger and believe in their abilities.

The Development Director is a full-time hybrid role based in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, with a combination of on-site and work-from-home responsibilities. This role leads the planning, execution, and evaluation of fundraising strategies, including campaigns, events, and donor initiatives to support Challenge Air’s mission and programs. Day-to-day tasks include cultivating and stewarding individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations; managing donor communications; preparing proposals and grant applications; and maintaining accurate fundraising records and reports. The Development Director will collaborate closely with the CEO/Executive Director and program staff to align development goals with organizational priorities, oversee budgets related to development activities, and support board members and volunteers in fundraising efforts. The role also involves representing the organization at community events and Fly Days, strengthening relationships with stakeholders, and identifying new opportunities for philanthropic support.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The Development Director will:
Develop and implement an annual fundraising and development plan.
Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors and prospective supporters.
Grow annual giving, recurring giving, major gift, and donor retention efforts.
Identify and develop corporate sponsorships and community partnerships.
Build relationships with donors, sponsors, foundations, service organizations, and community leaders.
Support foundation and grant fundraising efforts.
Manage donor communications, acknowledgments, stewardship, and recognition.
Maintain accurate donor and prospect information in the organization’s donor database/CRM.
Track fundraising progress and prepare reports to support planning and decision-making.
Work with the CEO/Executive Director, Board of Trustees, and volunteers to expand the organization’s fundraising reach.
Represent Challenge Air at Fly Days, community events, donor meetings, and networking opportunities.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Our ideal candidate is a confident and genuine relationship builder who enjoys connecting people with a meaningful mission. This person is strategic, organized, self-motivated, and comfortable working in a small nonprofit environment where everyone plays an important role.
Qualified candidates should have:
3 + years or more experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, sales, relationship management, or a related field.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Experience with donor databases, CRM systems, or similar technology.
The confidence and ability to cultivate donors and make direct fundraising asks.
The ability to work independently while collaborating closely with staff, board members, and volunteers.
A genuine commitment to the mission of Challenge Air for Kids & Friends.

WHY JOIN CHALLENGE AIR?

This is an opportunity to play a significant role in the growth of a national nonprofit organization with a unique and inspiring mission. The Development Director will have the opportunity to build relationships with donors and partners across the country while helping ensure that more children with special needs experience the confidence, joy, and possibilities created through the gift of flight.

To Apply:
Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in the position and relevant fundraising or relationship-development experience to HR @challengeair.org
.

Application Deadline: November 1, 2026

Salary Range: $65,000-$75,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications

Benefits: PTO, insurance, hybrid office position

Challenge Air for Kids & Friends, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Loomwork, an AI automation venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Loomwork is an AI automation agency for growing companies. Every growing company knows AI is its next growth lever, but few have the people to turn it into working systems. Implementation is the scarce resource. Loomwork helps them find where AI will pay off, builds agents into the tools they already use, and keeps those agents running. It launches as a services business with a dedicated technical delivery team from day one. Every engagement also serves as research: as client work converges on one segment, Loomwork turns its library of deployed agents into a connected product and grows from agency to software company.

Market Context

The global AI consulting services market is valued at $11.9B in 2026 and is projected to reach $73.9B by 2034, growing at a 25.6% CAGR. North America holds about 38% of the market. Enterprise AI adoption climbed from 20% in 2017 to 88% in 2025, and adoption is outpacing the talent available to deploy it. Roughly 190,000 US and Canadian companies fall in the $10M to $300M revenue range, which puts the serviceable market at an estimated $3B a year. Most of these companies are too large for freelancers and too small for enterprise firms.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
Investor and advisor network across the industry and early-stage capital markets
A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the direction of the venture and lead its execution.

Strategy: Shape the service offering, pricing, and positioning, and choose the segment to specialize in based on where demand converges
Customer Development: Win engagements with growing companies, move clients from assessment to build to retainer, and build the go-to-market motion
Product: Partner with the FutureSight delivery and engineering team to turn repeated client builds into reusable agents and, ultimately, a connected product
Capital: Lead future fundraising, supported by FutureSight's network and the agency's traction
Team: Recruit and lead the founding team, including a technical leader as the product takes shape, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
Direct exposure to AI implementation, consulting, or selling technology services into growing companies

How To Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.
